# Agent Office CLI monitor selective release

Release SHA:        a79d0a8bf3a6d15fb939d25acbe2f8a84a910dd8

This identifies the application candidate.
The final RC is the release PR head including this record.

- Main base / observed serving rollback SHA: `2f633a2333e8aaf84650cfe1c5aae5acf7c0f9b4`.
- Selected source: #3002, develop merge `de6dfde59e5facfefff2448680720d16cb2abda1`.
- The merge-commit cherry-pick applied without conflict. The selected feature's
  21 files, six files fixing unconfigured Test cron startup, and this release
  record are included. The startup correction does not enable either cron.
- Main advanced through #2999 and #3001 while RC validation was pending. Their
  changes were merged without conflict; the monitor's owner authorization, reauthentication,
  secret scanner and polling helpers are unchanged. The final RC includes this base.
- The owner explicitly authorized PR creation, merge, deployment and activation
  of the `codex-impl` collector on 2026-10-25, then selected a standalone release
  instead of the shared train. This is the authority for this release path.

Clicking `codex-impl` in Agent Office opens the approved read-only monitor for
its current conversation, tool output and terminal viewport. There is no
command input or worker-control endpoint. A dedicated ingest-only credential
feeds bounded, masked snapshots into volatile application memory. Only a
recently authenticated owner can read them. The app requires one replica;
snapshots expire after 15 minutes and no transcript history is persisted.

The single collector reads existing loopback AMUX endpoints. It sends no
worker prompt and makes no model call. It runs as a separate operator UID,
enforced by `ConditionUser`, in a Bubblewrap sandbox with a minimal read-only
filesystem and private process namespace. It receives no product database,
provider, bridge or worker credential. It remains disabled until production
serves the release.
